newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU refers Rheinmetall deal to Germany.
newsitem.headline: EU refers Rheinmetall deal to Germany.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday it had asked the German cartel office to examine the impact on the armoured vehicles market of a plan by German defence group Rheinmetall AG and British Aerospace Plc to take over STN Atlas.

Rheinmetall, together with German utility Badenwerk AG, last December signed a contract to buy 51 percent of German electronics company STN Atlas Elektronic GmbH. British Aerospace signed up to buy the remaining 49 percent.

German authorities had asked the Commission to refer the deal to the cartel office, saying it threatened to give Rheinmetall a dominant poisition in the market for "systems leadership" of armoured vehicles.

The European Union executive agreed the cartel authority should investigate that aspect of the linkup, noting that it had received complaints from market participants "which went in the same direction".
It said the deal's impact on other markets -- marine technology, systems technology and short-range air defence systems -- posed no problems under EU competition law.
"Apart from these (armoured vehicle) markets, the proposed concentration would not lead to the creation or strengthening of a dominant market position," it said in a statement.

The Commission has the authority to vet large mergers or acquisitions, but at the request of EU governments may refer cases back to national authorities if they affect competition primarily in national markets. -- Brussels newsroom, 322 287 6800
